text:
frank: FYI SAST CI started failing after recent key ACL tighten. error: KMS decrypt denied when scanner tries to fetch test fixtures.
nina: seeing same: job `sast-ci/2026-06-12-02` -> `403 AccessDenied: decrypt` from keystore.
priya: that was part of the RBAC hardening PR (PR #1499). we narrowed key bindings to service owners only. might've cut scanner SAs.
devsec-bot: Alert: KMS_DECRYPT_DENIED signature KMS_MISSING_KEY_BINDING impacted repos: redwood-core, redwood-web.
carla: i'm owner of the sdlc keys. i'm online, can do a scoped grant but let's do a checklist first. who needs access?
frank: ephemeral agents + ci-runner: `serviceAccount:ci-scanner@redwood-inference`, `serviceAccount:scan-agent-pod@redwood-inference`. both attempt decrypt in different contexts.
oliver: mitigation options:
- quick: add key binding for both SAs (fast, temporary)
- safer: add exception in RBAC PR with test plan + preflight job for future changes
- fallback: run offline scanner without keystore (manual, slow)
priya: prefer quick grant + add automation. can carla add and annotate audit log?
carla: doing scoped grant now, will add audit note and open follow-up to automate preflight.
devsec-bot: Audit Event: role.bind key=projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/sdlc/cryptoKeys/scan-key boundTo=[serviceAccount:ci-scanner@redwood-inference,serviceAccount:scan-agent-pod@redwood-inference] by carla@redwood.com ts=5187654352
nina: reran pipeline -> artifacts produced. one noisy high SAST match in `inference/sdk/loader.py` flagged as path-traversal. stack shows call to `os.path.join` + earlier `validate_relpath()` sanitization.
frank: that feels like a false positive at static level. but we should record runtime evidence before closing.
priya: propose triage workflow update: when FP suspected, attach runtime evidence (unit test or integration run) and label `security:fp-provisional`. only security can flip to `security:fp-confirmed`. automation should post template comment with repro steps.
oliver: for suppressions: add sanitized suppression comment style `# security-suppress: RULE_ID <jira-ticket>` and require a linked ticket. enforcement: pre-merge CI job rejects `security-suppress` without ticket.
carla: agree. I'll add to RBAC change checklist: 1) list affected keys and SAs, 2) run `keystore-preflight` in both runner and pod contexts, 3) include rollback command snippet in PR description.
nina: can we implement `keystore-preflight` as a tiny job that decrypts `sdlc-test-blob` and returns a structured exit code so we fail fast? something like:
```
# in runner context
keystore decrypt --key $SCANNER_KEY --ciphertext sample.ct || exit 42
# in ephemeral pod context run the same command as the pod SA
```
frank: add that to `.gitlab-ci.yml` under `check:keystore` and make it mandatory for RBAC PRs.
priya: follow-ups: (1) carla add key binding (done), (2) frank open automation PR for suppression enforcement, (3) nina add `keystore-preflight` job, (4) carla update RBAC playbook + changelog entry, (5) pr ticket for triage label automation.
devsec-bot: Action created: TASK-5072 created by carla@redwood.com "Add keystore preflight and RBAC PR checklist" ts=5187654396
frank: opened PR #1524 for suppression enforcement + comment template.
nina: I'll start `keystore-preflight` MR, will test locally against staging keystore emulator first.
priya: for the FP in loader.py, i'll add provisional label and attach unit test proving validate_relpath prevents exploit. then we'll move to `fp-confirmed` if test passes.
carla: thanks. let's also add an audit requirement: any key ACL change must be accompanied by a one-line changelog entry in `SECURITY_CHANGELOG.md` listing keys and SAs affected.
oliver: sounds good. closing thread after TASK-5072 merged and triage labels automated. :thumbsup:
